divisions.label: R Division
divisions.name: Representations
divisions.blurb: Encodings, equivalences, grammars, and what survives translation.
interests: Column-height vectors, w/h notation, and the tower word, a generalized Dyck grammar.
Lattice-path and permutation-cycle readings, with the two-line array and Foata intercalation as the classical grounding.
Polyomino embedding, and the castle graph as an encoding rather than an object.
Substructures: strips, snippets, and proper projections between heights.
Decision diagrams: the set of valid castles as a BDD or ZDD, with rank, unrank, uniform sampling, and intersection of castle families.
Real signals as castles: a URL id, an ID3 label, a waveform, an image row.
The codec ladder (WAV, FLAC, MP3; PNG, JPEG) as a ladder of compression tiers, and a lossless castle codec as a specification.
Compression and entropy: what the parity condition costs in bits, and whether it survives castle by castle.
Equivalences and translation loss: which invariants each encoding keeps and which it drops.

divisions.label: E Division
divisions.name: Enumeration
divisions.blurb: Counting methods, generating functions, recurrences, and sampling.
interests: Tower recursion, and the transfer matrix as the count that fits on one blackboard.
Sign and parity via roots of unity; the castle count as an upgraded cycle count.
Recurrence machinery: Kitamasa's method, Berlekamp-Massey, minimal recurrence order, and closed forms for P(k, L).
Convex counting by Vandermonde: every castle sits over a unique convex core, the fiber is a product of tower counts, and F(w, h) is a sum over convex castles.
The sign as a character: (T ± P)/2, roots of unity, the skyline DFT, and periods mod p as four uses of one orthogonality theorem; the Fourier spectrum of (−1)blocks on Zhw.
Generation: Knuth's Algorithm M, castle Gray codes, loopless enumerators, rank and unrank.
Tours of castle space: Hamilton paths on the move graph of V(w, h), SimPath ZDDs, Ruskey's polyomino and antimatroid Gray codes, and Viennot's heaps of pieces on the tower heap.
Brute force as ground truth: the Project Euler 502 enumerator and its limits.

divisions.label: N Division
divisions.name: Numbers
divisions.blurb: Sequences, exact arithmetic, difficult scales, and numerical patterns.
interests: Metallic means, the Pell strip, and the ladder of metallic means that strips can realize.
Perron roots, reachable number fields, and the Pisot/Salem question for cubics.
Continued fractions, convergents, and a crosswalk from eigenvalues to OEIS entries.
Bounded-height nacci sequences and their periods modulo primes.
Exact arithmetic at scale: the Project Euler 502 targets and modular reduction.
The Hardin word identity, A005251, and the missing sign-reversing involution.
Castle counts as integers: sums of three cubes and the residue mod 9, F(6, 4) = 1729 and Ramanujan's near-miss C-finite families, and Carmichael and perfect numbers as castle counts.
Symmetry of the signed transfer matrix: the commutant of Mk, the parity sectors of chark, and cyclic sieving at q = −1 on the tower Narayana numbers.
Units and lattices: metallic means as fundamental units, Perron roots located in the unit group of their field, and the minimum-height law as a lattice-point question.

divisions.label: Z Division
divisions.name: Zoo
divisions.blurb: Specimens, taxonomy, comparative morphology, and public interpretation.
interests: Taxonomy: geometric versus non-geometric classification, and the lattice of sub-families (convex, valley, tree, stack, Ferrers, parallelogram, prime).

Rule variations: tower spacing (skylines as window-g running minima, Hardin's min-of-g-adjacent tables), gap rules, no-touching, vertical spacing, and higher dimensions with the block count taken over superlevel components.
Symmetry across the census: mirror, cyclic shift, the dihedral group, and Burnside counts of shapes up to reflection.
Signal specimens: DTMF and MF tones as exactly periodic castles, and image rows and waveforms placed in the zoo.
Specimens: the 10-cell and 11-cell isospectral pairs, the golden and silver castles, the bronze hole.
Comparative morphology: the convex core (a unique hull above, no unique skeleton below), unimodal versus convex, and cousins from statistical physics.
Public interpretation: eigenvalues by example, and other guided tours of the zoo.

divisions.label: Q Division
divisions.name: q-Analogues
divisions.blurb: Area gradings, q-generating functions, joint statistics, and the bijections that preserve area.
interests: Area as a grading: castles by area, tree castles by area, bounded-height rows by area.

Prime castles (free-monoid primes in the sense of Gessel and Li) and the P/(1 − P) identity, with the Deutsch-Elizalde transport of Dyck-path primes; in the signed version, blocks − 1 is a monoid homomorphism and the sign is a character of the free monoid on primes.
The q-polyomino zoo: Bousquet-Mélou's add-a-column generating functions read at the area variable, with A001169 and A001523 as landmarks.
Classical q-families: Carlitz q-Catalan, Barcucci q-Motzkin and q-Bessel, weakly unimodal compositions, steep polyominoes.
Bistatistics: area together with block count, peaks, and records; hunting for q-binomial and Narayana-q coefficients.
Bijections: tree castles versus all castles by area at h = 3, and convex to valley cell by cell in (w, h).

divisions.label: S Division
divisions.name: Spectra
divisions.blurb: Castle graphs, transfer and kernel eigenvalues, isospectral pairs, and what a castle sounds like.
interests: Five spectra: the transfer matrix, the LGV kernel, the skyline DFT, the combinatorial Laplacian, and the Ihara zeta function.
The castle graph: bipartite and planar, with cycle rank equal to the number of 2 × 2 blocks; tree castles by height.
Spectral radius: λ1 = h for the count, metallic radii of individual castles, and the search for a bronze one.
Isospectrality: Kac's drum, the exhaustive census up to 16 cells, and Sunada constructions.
Universality: the sine-kernel bulk, GUE, and random Young tableaux via the LGV kernel.
Expanders and zeta: Ramanujan castles, prime closed walks, and arithmetic combinatorics.

Signals: the skyline DFT as a complete invariant, compressed sensing, and turnpike reconstruction; the Woodward gap, where a skyline played as a tone has a spectrum that approaches its height histogram at a rate set by the block count.

Sandpiles in two models (the sink model, with one sink cell, and the tide model, with the base row as the sink): the 2 × 2 squares as a basis of the cycle lattice, the sandpile group from the Smith normal form of the Laplacian, spanning trees, the identity element, the period of a grain dropped on the apex, and Bak-Tang-Wiesenfeld avalanche statistics as candidate invariants.

divisions.label: T Division
divisions.name: Transcendentals
divisions.blurb: Samplers, limit laws, geometric probability, and π drawn out of castle ensembles.
interests: The sampler toolkit: ten techniques, from rejection sampling to coupling from the past and Wang-Landau.
Central limit routes: a castle statistic, its normal limit, and π from the density at the mode.
Random matrix routes: the semicircle, Tracy-Widom, the Airy edge, Marchenko-Pastur, Kesten-McKay.
Geometric probability: Buffon's needle across a skyline, Barbier's theorem, and Ehrhart theory on the castle polytope.
Classical identities in castle asymptotics: Stirling, Basel, Wallis.
Random walks on castle graphs: return, cover, and hitting times; loop-erased walks and conformal invariance.
Beyond π: Catalan's constant G, ζ(3), and γ; and the wall between algebraic and transcendental numbers as the reason any of this is hard.

divisions.label: F Division
divisions.name: Fractional
divisions.blurb: Non-integer orders, power-law memory, interpolated statistics, and dense operators where the integer castle has sparse ones.
interests: Three definitions on three castle objects: Grünwald-Letnikov on skylines (binomially weighted column differences), Riemann-Liouville on generating functions ((1 − x)−α), and Caputo on recurrences (initial terms preserved).

Interpolated statistics: a fractional block count Bα with area and block count as its endpoints; Z(q, α) joining the area generating function to the Narayana block polynomial, and as a cell fingerprint; two irrational orders as injective coordinates for a castle.

Interpolated arguments: fractional width via Mw−1 and fractional height via the quasi-polynomial in k; the parity condition as a branch cut; the half-column embedding problem and its poset theorem (a nonnegative half-column exists exactly when the rule is a partial order); fractional width as bit cost; the boundary defect of the semigroup law at the wall.

Fractional sums and transforms: Cesàro half-sums and the √π in Γ(1/2); Mittag-Leffler generating functions between ordinary and exponential; fractional recurrences and the constants no strip realizes.
Anomalous diffusion on the castle graph: the comb model and time-fractional order 1/2; Lévy flights and the space-fractional Laplacian; fractional heat traces.
Long memory: Hurst exponents and ARFIMA orders of real skylines, and strip rules with power-law memory and their dense truncated transfer matrices.
Fractional powers in finite rings: roots of xw in Fp[x]/(char) and the half-step oracle.

divisions.label: X Division
divisions.name: Ciphers
divisions.blurb: Keystreams, hidden payloads, commitments, and what survives an adversary.
interests: Castle keystreams: LFSRs, ring arithmetic over Fp[x], linear complexity, and the attacks that break them.
Steganography on skylines: LSB payloads, block-parity carriers, and capacity per castle.
The castle as a channel: real image rows read as carriers, and how they degrade under cropping, scaling, and re-encoding.
Commitments: whether the parity condition makes a castle a natural commitment scheme, and which invariants an opening reveals.

Adversarial models: what a distinguisher sees when castles are drawn from two rules with the same spectrum, and when isospectrality becomes a security parameter; a warden who counts blocks, and the joint statistics that could catch a block-parity carrier.

Analog channels and in-band signaling: which castle statistics survive an FM voice channel; the parity condition as control computed from data, and the edits that move the skyline without flipping it.

Integrity without a key: a keyed fractional phase broken with three known castles; a public-order phase as an integrity check; the castle ring by invariant factors, with Pohlig-Hellman as the structure theorem.
Hardness candidates: castle problems (the isospectrality census, height reconstruction, turnpike) as sources of one-way functions.

divisions.label: C Division
divisions.name: Chinese Remainder Theorem
divisions.blurb: The Chinese Remainder Theorem applied to castle rings: idempotents, local factors, periods, and attacks.
interests: The theorem in ring form: comaximal ideals, the product isomorphism, and the integer CRT as a special case.
Idempotent decompositions: orthogonal idempotents as the inverse of the CRT map, and eigenvalue sectors of the castle ring.
The castle ring mod p: Fp[x]/(chark) split along the factors of chark, periods as least common multiples over the factors, and unit groups and invariant factors.
Local factors and prime powers: repeated factors at primes dividing the discriminant, nilradicals, and moduli such as Z/9 that do not split.
The castle ring over the integers: parity sectors over Q, Spec Z[x]/(chark) and its fibers, and lifting idempotents.
CRT in cryptanalysis: Pohlig-Hellman on the ring and on the exponent, against a castle Diffie-Hellman.

divisions.label: M Division
divisions.name: Metallurgy
divisions.blurb: Golden, silver, and bronze means and the higher rungs δ<sub>4</sub>, δ<sub>5</sub>, ..., the plastic ratio, Fibonacci castles, and families that grow like a metallic mean.
interests: Fibonacci castles: Fibonacci towers, the Fibonacci Q-matrix as a transfer matrix, the Fibonacci word, and Zeckendorf ranking.
Ridge castles: the ridge rule, its transfer matrix, and its growth constants up the metallic ladder.
The metallic rungs: golden through δ<sub>5</sub> as continued fractions, their convergents in the OEIS, and which rungs a castle strip rule can realize.
The golden, silver, and plastic ratios, and families that are metallic by count, by width, by area, or by spectrum.

divisions.label: B Division
divisions.name: Bioinformatics
divisions.blurb: Biological sequences, molecular folding, structure counts, and the combinatorics computational biology shares with castles.
interests: RNA secondary structures: Deutsch and Elizalde's bijection from no-double-rise bargraphs of semiperimeter n + 1 to secondary structures on n vertices; its mirror, the castles that drop by at most 1 and end at height 1, counted by semiperimeter as A004148, the RNA sequence.

divisions.label: The Telephone Company
divisions.name: The Telephone Company
divisions.blurb: Phone signals, audio codecs, tone catalogs, and the information theory of skylines.
interests: Waveform codecs: LPC plus Rice coding on a peak-normalized song waveform; the castle codec (a skyline as a simple rule plus a residual) as a specification; the codec ladder (WAV, FLAC, MP3, AAC, Opus) as a ladder of tiers on a real signal.
Tone castles: DTMF and MF digits at 8 kHz as exactly periodic castles, with their DFT support and Goertzel response; which tone pairs are exactly periodic and which only approximately.

Skyline as tone: a column-height sequence encoded as an instantaneous-frequency tone, whose spectrum approaches the height histogram (Woodward's theorem) at a rate set by the block count; an audio-spectral analogue of the isospectral census.

Hearing the shape: Kac's question, the 10-cell adjacency-isospectral pair and the 11-cell Laplacian-isospectral tree pair, Sunada-style constructions, and whether the Ihara zeta function or the skyline DFT separates what adjacency does not.
Expanders and zeta: Ramanujan castles as the shapes that behave most like expanders, and ζC(u) over prime closed walks on the castle graph.
Voice-channel survival: which castle statistics (low bit of height, block parity, histogram bins, low DFT modes) survive FM demodulation on a band-limited voice channel.
Information theory of skylines: uniform entropy of about w log2 h − 1 bits, growth constants as topological entropies, and the compressibility axis.
Constrained coding: run-length-limited sequences as castle towers, the Shannon capacity of a constraint, and line codes from recording and telephony.

Real signals as castles: URL ids, ID3 labels, and 16-bit waveforms as castles of height 65536; Berlekamp-Massey and the number-theoretic transform over F65537 as the finite-field layer; Beethoven's Ninth as the showcase example.

divisions.label: Facilities
divisions.name: Facilities
divisions.blurb: Real objects turned into castles: keys, city skylines, mountain ridgelines, ballparks.
interests: Keys as castles: pin-tumbler bitting read as column heights, photographs of keys converted to castles, and standard key blanks (pin positions, depths, maximum adjacent cut) as castle families with countable keyspaces.

Skylines and ridgelines: famous city skylines and mountain ranges (national parks, and city backdrops such as the mountains behind Salt Lake City) read as castles, and zooming in on them as a way into fractals and the coastline paradox.

Ballparks: each ray out from home plate as a castle (field, wall, stands); the bare field-and-wall ray as a hook castle; overhanging decks, which the no-overhang rule removes; and a park as a fan of castles, compared across the 30 MLB parks.

PE502-1.summary: A self-contained introduction: castles and their blocks, a one-line count of all castles, and the parity condition handled by weighting each castle with a sign.
PE502-1.abstract: A castle is a bargraph polyomino: a row of columns standing on a common base, one of which reaches a given ceiling. Project Euler Problem 502 asks how many castles on a w × h grid are built from an even number of blocks, for grids as large as 1012 in one dimension. This report is a self-contained introduction. It defines castles and their blocks, counts all castles in one line, and then shows how the parity condition is handled by weighting each castle with a sign. The result is a closed form for the even-block count in terms of a signed tower count whose generating function is rational, which is what makes the trillion-scale evaluations cheap.

PE502-2.summary: Castles of exact height 2 with no two neighboring columns at the ceiling number Fw+2 − 1 at width w. Transfer matrices, Zeckendorf ranks, block parity, and ridge castles up the metallic ladder.
PE502-2.abstract: A Fibonacci castle is a castle of exact height 2 in which no two neighboring columns both reach the ceiling. There are Fw+2 − 1 of them at width w, where Fj is the j-th Fibonacci number, so their number grows like a constant times φw, with φ the golden ratio. Project Euler Problem 502 asks how many castles have an even number of blocks. For the Fibonacci castles of width w the answer is half their number plus half a signed count, which adds +1 for each even-block castle and −1 for each odd-block castle. This signed count takes only the values 0, 1 and 2 and repeats with period 6 in w, while over all castles of exact height 2 it is unbounded. We also derive Fibonacci identities from Fibonacci castles and rank them by the Zeckendorf representation of integers. Ridge castles, in which neighboring columns differ in height unless both reach the ceiling, grow like φw at height 2 and like the metallic mean of order h − 1 at height h. Two more families grow like φn when castles are counted by their number n of cells: all castles of exact height 2, and prime castles, which have no column of height 1.

PE502-3.abstract: The rational function x/(1 − 2x − x2) generates the Pell numbers P⋆n, and the coefficients of 1/(1 − 2x − x2) are the same numbers shifted by one place, P⋆n+1. This report shows that they count castle skylines: the skylines on the heights 1, 2, 3 that start at height 1 and change by at most one between neighboring columns number P⋆w at width w. Requiring the skyline to reach height 3 gives the Pell castles, a castle family of height 3 with APell(w) = P⋆w − 2w−1 members, which grows like the silver ratio 1 + √2. Split by the parity of their number of blocks, the Pell castles fall into two halves up to a term of size O(3w/2). The silver ratio is the second of the metallic means, after the golden ratio of the Fibonacci castles of PE502-2. On the heights 1, 2, 3 the ridge rule of PE502-2 has the same growth constant as the Pell rule and the same number of skylines with a free first column, but not the same number of castles of height 3.
